source_quotes.condition_other: Vincristine-induced neuropathic pain (VIN) is thought to result from damage to the microtubule organization of neuronal axons (Tanner et al., 1998; Pan et al., 2003).
source_quotes.species: The study employed male Sprague-Dawley rats (200–300 g; Taconic Farms Germantown, NY, USA) that had free access to food and water and were maintained on a 12-h light/dark cycle throughout the study.
source_quotes.sham_type: Sham animals underwent surgery and anesthesia needed for liFUS but received no liFUS treatment. This generated four test cohorts consisting of: Vin/liFUS, saline/liFUS, VIN/sham liFUS and saline/sham liFUS.
source_quotes.anaesthesia: Before liFUS treatment, 5% isofluorane was administered through a vaporizer to induce anesthesia via nose cone (Braintree Scientific Inc., MA, USA). Animals were maintained under anesthesia at 2% isofluorane.
source_quotes.adverse_events: Possible tissue damage due to internal or external liFUS treatment to the DRG was evaluated postmortem using H&E staining. Both treatments, 24 and 120 h postliFUS, showed no sign of pyknosis or edema in the tissue.
source_quotes.safety_notes: Possible tissue damage due to internal or external liFUS treatment to the DRG was evaluated postmortem using H&E staining. Both treatments, 24 and 120 h postliFUS, showed no sign of pyknosis or edema in the tissue.

flags.reason: Total combines the internal liFUS cohort (n=27: VIN/liFUS 12, saline/liFUS 5, VIN/sham 5, saline/sham 5) and external liFUS cohort (n=25: VIN/liFUS 8, saline/liFUS 7, VIN/sham 5, saline/sham 5); only about 32 of these 52 animals (the liFUS, non-sham groups) received active ultrasound, the remainder were sham-treated controls.

The text states the pulse is '38 Hz with a period of 90 ns', but 90 ns corresponds to the period of the 11 MHz carrier, not to a 38 Hz repetition period (which would be ~26 ms); recorded both stated numbers verbatim without reconciling the apparent inconsistency.

Only acoustic power in Watts (2.5 W internal, 8 W external) is given; no spatial-peak intensity (W/cm2) or pressure value is reported for either exposure, so all pressure/intensity fields are not_reported.

Sham animals underwent the same surgery/anesthesia as treated animals but received no liFUS; classified as inactive_transducer as the closest match, though the paper does not explicitly say the transducer was present but unpowered.

condition_other: Vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy (chemotherapy-induced neuropathic pain model)
readout_other: Von Frey filament mechanical withdrawal threshold (VFF); hot plate thermal nociceptive threshold (HPT); open field locomotor test (OFT); thermocouple temperature recording at the DRG; Hematoxylin & Eosin and Fluorojade histology of the DRG
direction_notes: liFUS treatment of the L5 DRG reversed vincristine-induced mechanical (VFF) and thermal (HPT) nociceptive hypersensitivity toward pre-vincristine baseline levels for up to 5 days, without affecting locomotion (OFT) or causing histological damage.
safety_notes: Both treatments, 24 and 120 h postliFUS, showed no sign of pyknosis or edema in the tissue.

timing.protocol_description: Internal liFUS treatment was administered at 2.5 W for 3 minutes with 11 MHz, pulsed at 38 Hz with a period of 90 ns, and a pulse width of 13 ms, applied via a laminectomy-exposed probe placed directly on the DRG. A single liFUS treatment was given, with behavioral testing pre-treatment and at 24, 48, 72 and 120 h post-treatment.

External liFUS was administered at 8 W for 3 min with 11 MHz, pulsed at 38 Hz with a period of 90 ns, and a pulse width of 13 ms, delivered non-invasively through the skin with the transducer positioned over the posterior superior iliac spine and aimed at the DRG under VEVO 3100 ultrasound image guidance. A single liFUS treatment was given, with behavioral testing pre-treatment and at 24, 48, 72 and 120 h post-treatment.
